findings.F1: The market did the opposite of the idea: on the 5-day grid, the coin's 5-day return net of its drift, signed away from the middle of its 30-day range, was +0.61 % (t 2.91, n 2555). It was +0.30 % at 1 day (t 3.11), +0.50 % at 3 days (t 3.01), +1.26 % at 10 days (t 3.97, overlapping on the 5-day grid), and on a non-overlapping 10-day grid +1.09 % (t 2.53, n 1259). So moves away from the middle continued instead of reverting.
findings.F2: Flatness did not strengthen reversion and did not clearly change the continuation. At 10 days, the flatter half continued +1.37 % (t 2.47, n 629) and the less-flat half +0.80 % (t 1.22, n 630), with Welch t 0.67. At 5 days, the trendiest flatness quartile continued +0.24 % (t 0.48) against +0.69 % to +0.80 % (t 1.8 to 2.0) in the other three.
findings.F3: The continuation was carried by closes far above the middle. In the highest quintile of signed distance, the 10-day return net of drift was +2.98 % (t 2.32, n 252). The other four quintiles ranged from -0.43 % to -1.02 % (all |t| ≤ 1.1). Distance alone ranked the 10-day move only weakly (Spearman 0.038; OLS slope on distance t 0.93).
findings.F4: The continuation changed sign across periods. The 10-day continuation was +4.44 % in 2020 (t 3.49) and +3.26 % in 2021 (t 2.06). It turned to reversion in 2022 (-1.98 %, t -2.03) and 2023 (-1.80 %, t -2.12). Only 58 % of coin-windows were positive.
findings.F5: By coin, the 10-day continuation sat in ETH (+2.03 %, t 2.23), XRP (+2.30 %, t 1.69) and ZEC (+1.65 %, t 1.27). BTC, LTC and XMR were near zero (+0.16 % to +0.21 %, t ≤ 0.27).
findings.F6: The 5-day continuation held on both sides: +0.63 % above the middle (t 1.99, n 1239) and +0.59 % below it (t 2.13, n 1316). A plain 30-day momentum sign gave a similar +0.54 % over 5 days (t 2.60) and +0.89 % over 10 days (t 2.80).
findings.F7: The tested reversion lost -0.40 % per case over 5 days (strength -0.039, 2912 cases), against a trade cost of 0.19 %. The opposite move, continuation, is about +0.61 % per case over 5 days and about +1.1 % over 10 days. That is roughly 3 to 6 times the cost.

ideas.idea: The closer a coin's daily close sits to the top of its 30-day closing range, the more the coin rises over the next 10 days.
ideas.consequence: A close pressed against the top of the past month's range is a reason to be long the following days, not to sell it back toward the middle.
ideas.name: near-range-top continuation

ideas.idea: The farther a coin's daily close sits from the middle of its 30-day closing range, the more the coin keeps moving in that direction over the next 10 days, up from above the middle and down from below it.
ideas.consequence: A trader should not fade moves away from the middle of a month's range, and can lean with them instead.
ideas.name: range-distance continuation ten days
